title: Household Timekeeping Stability Survey
researchQuestion: What patterns of agreement appear among commonly available clocks during routine indoor use over a fourteen-day interval?
summary: This study looks at how ordinary clocks and time displays agree or drift over two weeks. Participants describe each device by broad category only; no brands, serial numbers, network records, or exact locations are requested.
commitment: Two observations weekly for fourteen days
eligibility: Routine access to at least three independently operating time displays.
One display must provide a network-synchronized or radio-controlled reference.
Able to observe the same displays without moving or resetting them during the study interval.
exclusions: Workplace control systems, security systems, medical equipment, and restricted equipment are excluded.
No account information, network logs, device identifiers, photographs, or precise location information are requested.
participantActivities: Assign a simple device category to each participating display and identify one reference display.
Twice each week, read the displays in the same order and record whole-minute agreement or difference from the reference.
Note only ordinary interruptions such as a power loss, manual reset, daylight-saving adjustment, or device replacement.

protocolSteps.title: Inventory
protocolSteps.description: Select three to six ordinary time displays and assign each a broad device category.

protocolSteps.title: Reference
protocolSteps.description: Designate one synchronized display as the comparison reference for the full interval.

protocolSteps.title: Compare
protocolSteps.description: Read all selected displays in the same order twice each week.

protocolSteps.title: Close
protocolSteps.description: Record ordinary resets or interruptions and complete the final agreement check.

dataRequested: Number of available clocks within the permitted range.
Broad clock categories and the type of synchronized reference.
Whole-minute differences observed on the assigned schedule.
Fixed-category notes for power interruption or manual adjustment.
dataNotRequested: Names, contact details, account information, or household identifiers.
Brands, model numbers, serial numbers, network addresses, or photographs.
Exact time zone, street address, coordinates, or device telemetry.
samplePrompts: How many selected displays agree with the reference to the displayed minute?
Has any selected display been reset since the previous observation?
Were all displays read in the assigned order?
methodNotes: Comparisons use displayed whole minutes rather than sub-second timing, which keeps the method suitable for ordinary household equipment.
The same synchronized display remains the reference throughout the interval unless it becomes unavailable; reference changes close the series.
Device descriptions are categorical so the study does not create an inventory of a participant's household equipment.
limitations: Display update behavior and synchronization methods vary by device category.
Reading order introduces a small interval between the first and last comparison.
The survey describes displayed agreement and does not provide calibration or product-performance certification.

application.title: Eligibility check
application.introduction: Tell us which types of time displays you have and whether the two-week schedule works for you. Completing this check gives you a reference number but does not enroll you.

fields.label: I confirm that I am 18 years of age or older.
Number of ordinary time displays available

fields.label: I can complete two scheduled observations each week for fourteen days.
